verses.english: Linked Discourses 7.22
2. Lay Followers
At Khomadussa
So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati khomadussaṁ nāmaṁ sakyānaṁ nigamo.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, where they have a town named Khomadussa.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya khomadussaṁ nigamaṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
verses.english: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Khomadussa for alms.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā sabhāyaṁ sannipatitā honti kenacideva karaṇīyena, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyati.
verses.english: Now at that time the brahmins and householders of Khomadussa were gathered in the council hall for some business, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā yena sā sabhā tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then the Buddha approached that council.

verses.pali: Addasaṁsu khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: The brahmins and householders saw the Buddha coming off in the distance,
and said,

verses.pali: “ke ca muṇḍakā samaṇakā, ke ca sabhādhammaṁ jānissantī”ti?
verses.english: “Who are these shavelings, these fake ascetics? Don’t they understand the council rules?”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā khomadussake brāhmaṇagahapatike gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha addressed the brahmins and householders of Khomadussa in verse:
“If good people are not present it is no true council;

verses.pali: Santo na te ye na vadanti dhammaṁ;
verses.english: and those whose speak against principle <j>are not good people.
Having given up greed, hate, and delusion,
speakers of principle are good people.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: When he had spoken, the brahmins and householders of Khomadussa said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent!

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
verses.english: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

verses.pali: Ete mayaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
verses.english: We go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Upāsake no bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṁ gate”ti.
verses.english: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life.”
The Linked Discourses with Brahmins are complete.
